title: Cryptic Alphanumeric Naming based on ASCII codes (e.g. `w44`)
damaged_code:
```rust
// Rust
fn w44(val: f64) -> String { ... } // w stands for "with", 44 is ASCII for comma
```
pattern: Naming functions or types with cryptic combinations of letters and numbers representing raw ASCII values.
why_bad: It is completely non-obvious and relies on obscure, tribal trivia. A developer is forced to look up an ASCII chart to deduce that `44` represents a comma, creating an unnecessary hurdle for comprehension.
detection: Function or struct names combining characters and digits that map directly to common punctuation ASCII characters.
fix:
Rename the function to a descriptive term expressing the domain formatting action.
```rust
fn format_with_commas(val: f64) -> String { ... }
```
source: *Refactoring to Patterns*, Chapter 4 / *The Art of Readable Code*.
